claims.text: What the strip looks like Sinus tachy, a widened QRS, and a dom terminal R wave in aVR.
claims.quote: TCA Toxicity: Sinus tachycardia, widened QRS, dominant terminal R wave in aVR

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Rate: sinus tachy (usual; muscarinic M1-r blockade)
claims.quote: Patients with tricyclic overdose will also usually demonstrate sinus tachycardia secondary to muscarinic (M1) receptor blockade

claims.text: QRS: intraventricular conduction delay, QRS > 100 ms in lead II
claims.quote: Intraventricular conduction delay: QRS > 100 ms in lead II

claims.text: aVR: terminal R wave > 3 mm or R/S ratio > 0.7
claims.quote: Terminal R wave > 3 mm in aVR or R/S ratio > 0.7 in aVR

claims.text: QT: prolonged; aVR: dom 2/2 R′ wave > 3 mm
claims.quote: QT prolongation Dominant secondary R wave (R’) in aVR > 3mm

claims.text: Why aVR: the right-sided conducting system = more suscep to sodium-channel blockade, giving terminal Rt axis deviation of the QRS — the dom R′ in aVR
claims.quote: The right-sided intraventricular conducting system is more susceptible to the effects of sodium channel blockade — this causes terminal right axis deviation of the QRS complex, which manifests as a dominant R’ wave in aVR.

claims.text: QRS width predicts trouble: QRS > 100 ms predicts seizures; QRS > 160 ms predicts ventricular arrhythmias (ex, VT)
claims.quote: The degree of QRS broadening on ECG is correlated with adverse events: QRS > 100 ms is predictive of seizures QRS > 160 ms is predictive of ventricular arrhythmias (e.g. VT)

claims.text: → (mech and diagnoses) Mech: blockade of myocard fast sodium channels (wide QRS, tall R in aVR), inhibition of potassium channels (long QTc), and direct myocard depression
claims.quote: Tricyclics mediate their cardiotoxic effects via blockade of myocardial fast sodium channels (QRS prolongation, tall R wave in aVR), inhibition of potassium channels (QTc prolongation) and direct myocardial depression.

claims.text: Other toxic effects come from muscarinic (M1), histamine (H1) and α1-adrenergic-r blockade
claims.quote: Other toxic effects are produced by blockade at muscarinic (M1), histamine (H1) and α1-adenergic receptors.

claims.text: Sodium-channel blockers: tricyclic antidepressants (MC), type Ia antiarrhythmics (quinidine, procainamide), type Ic (flecainide, encainide), local anesthetics (bupivacaine, ropivacaine), antimalarials (chloroquine, hydroxychloroquine), dextropropoxyphene, propranolol, carbamazepine, quinine
claims.quote: Tricyclic antidepressants (= most common) Type Ia antiarrhythmics (quinidine, procainamide) Type Ic antiarrhythmics (flecainide, encainide) Local anaesthetics (bupivacaine, ropivacaine) Antimalarials (chloroquine, hydroxychloroquine) Dextropropoxyphene Propranolol Carbamazepine Quinine

claims.text: Take an ECG in every deliberate self-poisoning (or altered GCS of unknown cause) to screen for TCA OD
claims.quote: An ECG should be taken in all patients who present with a deliberate self-poisoning (or altered GCS of unknown aetiology) to screen for TCA overdose.

claims.text: Sx Rapid onset (w.in 1–2 hrs): sedation and coma, seizures, hypotension, tachy, broad-complex dysrhythmias, anticholinergic syndrome (tachy, mydriasis, dry mouth)
claims.quote: In overdose, the tricyclics produce rapid onset (within 1-2 hours) of: Sedation and coma Seizures Hypotension Tachycardia Broad complex dysrhythmias Anticholinergic syndrome (tachycardia, mydriasis, dry mouth)

claims.text: Tx of sig OD w cardiotoxicity OD > 10 mg/kg w ECG signs of cardiotoxicity: resuscitative mgnt in a monitored area equipped for airway mgnt
claims.quote: Overdose >10mg/kg with signs of cardiotoxicity (ECG changes) requires resuscitative management: Patients need to be managed in a monitored area equipped for airway management

claims.text: IV access, high-flow O2, monitoring
claims.quote: Secure IV access, administer high flow oxygen and attach monitoring equipment

claims.text: IV sodium bicarb — given correctly, as excess can cause iatrogenic death
claims.quote: Administer IV sodium bicarbonate. See our antidote post on the correct administration of sodium bicarbonate as excess can cause iatrogenic death.

claims.text: Intubate ASAP; hyperventilate to keep pH 7.50–7.55
claims.quote: Intubate as soon as possible Hyperventilate to maintain a pH of 7.50 – 7.55.

claims.text: Once the airway = secure: NGT and 50 g (1 g/kg) activated charcoal
claims.quote: Once the airway is secure, place a nasogastric tube and give 50g (1g/kg) of activated charcoal.

claims.text: Seizures: IV benzodiazepines (ex, midazolam 1–2 mg)
claims.quote: Treat seizures with IV benzodiazepines (e.g. midazolam 1-2mg)

claims.text: Hypotension: crystalloid bolus 10–20 mL/kg; if that fails, consider vasopressors (ex, noradrenaline infusion)
claims.quote: Treat hypotension with a crystalloid bolus (10-20 mL/kg). If this is unsuccessful in restoring BP then consider starting vasopressors (e.g. noradrenaline infusion)

claims.text: Arrhythmias: first give more sodium bicarb; lidocaine 1.5 mg/kg IV = third-line (after bicarb and hypervent) once pH = > 7.5
claims.quote: If arrhythmias occur, the first step is to give more sodium bicarbonate. Lidocaine (1.5mg/kg) IV is a third-line agent (after bicarbonate and hyperventilation) once pH is > 7.5

claims.text: ⍉class Ia (procainamide) and Ic (flecainide) antiarrhythmics, BBs and amiodarone — they may worsen hypotension and conduction abnormalities
claims.quote: Avoid Ia (procainamide) and Ic (flecainide) antiarrhythmics, beta-blockers and amiodarone as they may worsen hypotension and conduction abnormalities

claims.text: Admit to the ICU
claims.quote: Admit the patient to the intensive care unit for ongoing management
